{{short description|British mathematician and computer scientist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Bobby Hersom''' (born 1929 in [[Cheshire, England]]) is a British mathematician and computer scientist known for her early work on computers at [[Elliott Brothers (computer company)|Elliott Brothers]], [[Hatfield Polytechnic]], and the Rothamstead Agricultural Research Station.<ref name=ETHW>{{cite web |url=https://ethw.org/Oral-History:Bobby_Hersom |title=Oral-History:Bobby Hersom |website=[[Engineering and Technology History Wiki]] |author=Janet Abbate |author-link=Janet Abbate |date=20 September 2001 |accessdate=April 11, 2020 |archive-date=11 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411160935/https://ethw.org/Oral-History:Bobby_Hersom |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Life ==
Hersom was born Beryl Lewis (not Roberta as in <ref name=Lavington2>{{cite book |title=Early Computing in Britain: Ferranti Ltd. and Government Funding, 1948-1958 |first=Simon |last=Lavington |publisher=Springer |date=2019 |isbn=9783030151034 |page=360}}</ref>) in Cheshire, England, the oldest of three children. She earned a maths degree from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1950. She then earned a teaching degree in 1951.<ref name=ETHW /> She was a member of The Round, an English Country Dance Club while at Cambridge.<ref name=TheRound>{{cite web |url=https://round.soc.srcf.net/history/dynasty |title=The Round: Cambridge University English Country Dance Club |accessdate=April 11, 2020 |archive-date=12 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412030921/https://round.soc.srcf.net/history/dynasty |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Lavington>{{cite book |title=Moving Targets: Elliott-Automation and the Dawn of the Computer Age in Britain, 1947 – 67 |author=Simon Lavington |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |date=May 2011 |isbn=9781848829336}}</ref>{{rp|267}}

She married [[Ed Hersom]], who she met through work, in 1954.<ref name=Abbate>{{cite book |title=Recoding Gender: Women's Changing Participation in Computing |author=Janet Abbate |publisher=MIT Press |year=2012 |isbn=9780262304535}}</ref>{{rp|116}}

Her son Colin also attended Cambridge<ref name=TheRound /> and was a mathematician and her daughter was a farmer.<ref name=ETHW /> She regretted having to quit her work as a computer scientist after her first child was born, which meant she could only work freelance.<ref>{{cite book |title=Connecting Women: Women, Gender and ICT in Europe in the Nineteenth and Twentieth Century |chapter=The Gendering of the Computing Field in Finland, France and the United Kingdom Between 1960 and 1990 |date=December 2014 |isbn=9783319208374 |first1=Chantal |last1=Morley |first2=Martina |last2=McDonnell |chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/300338956 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-20837-4_8 |accessdate=2020-04-11}}</ref>

Her husband died in 2002.<ref name=Lavington />{{rp|302}}

== Career ==
After earning her teaching degree, Hersom worked as a teacher, but realized she didn't enjoy that work.<ref name=ETHW />

She started working in the Theory Division at Elliott Brothers in Borehamwood, UK, in 1953.<ref name=Lavington />{{rp|262, 267}} There she wrote software programs for Nicholas, a research computer. Some of the software she developed processed [[radar]] data.<ref name=ETHW /> In 1954, she left that job to start her family.<ref name=Abbate />{{rp|116}}<ref name=Lavington2 />

Hersom then worked for Rothamstead for 11 years.<ref name=ETHW /> She later worked as a consultant for [[Hatfield Polytechnic]], along with her husband. She worked there until retirement.<ref name=ETHW />
